newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse up, second tier bullish.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse up, second tier bullish.

text.p: Most Bucharest share prices closed higher on Thursday under buying pressure, which traders said had been stronger on the second tier.
"Investors targeted cheaper stocks today and we had significant average price rises, of up to 50 percent, on the lower tier," a trader said. "Also, the bulk of shares in this section closed firmer."
The upward price movement was expected to continue on Friday.
Nineteen of 38 second-tier stocks ended stronger, seven moved lower and seven remained unchanged. Four stocks had no trade and one was suspended.

On the first tier, three companies touched higher closing quotes, one slipped and two were flat. Refrigerator maker Arctic remained suspended pending privatisation and Azomures fertiliser maker was suspended in the morning after reporting it had a shareholders' meeting on Wednesday.
Volume was 2.7 million shares, up from 2.5 million, and turnover rose some 800 million lei to 13.5 billion. The first tier took more than 80 percent of total turnover.
Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, jumped by 1.42, 1.35 and 1.79 percent respectively from the previous session.

Gainers on the first tier included pharmaceuticals Antibiotice, which firmed 100 to close at 8,700, and Terapia, which was 1,300 lei up at 12,500. Sofert fertiliser maker ended 2,200 lei higher at 36,200.
Compa vehicle parts maker was the section's loser, weakening 100 lei to 2,700. Oltchim and Policolor chemicals were flat at 5,250 and 6,450 lei.
Armatura industrial fittings maker and carbide maker Carbid-Fox took the bulk of trading on the second tier.
